title: Driving and suppressing the human language network using large language models
goal: Reproduce the original selected performance result and meaningfully exceed the strongest relevant author comparator on exactly the same task: Original Figure 3 sentence-response prediction on all 1500 sentences and three original evaluation participants, preserving the baseline1000 companion and original participant-mean Pearson reduction.
primary_outputs: Executable source-indexed predictions and complete support accounting for Original Figure 3 sentence-response prediction on all 1500 sentences and three original evaluation participants, preserving the baseline1000 companion and original participant-mean Pearson reduction.
Independent reproduction comparison to authenticated source reference, including all specified original companions.
Independent same-task improvement comparison against strongest relevant published/refitted author comparator with meaningful paired uncertainty; both access conditions reported separately.
Separately named biological reproduction retained through unchanged predecessor contracts; no substituted model, cohort, split or metric.
success_criteria: Recreate the selected original performance result from authentic complete source inputs; reported-score copying alone is insufficient.
Use the same source data, target/input information, original split, metric and complete declared output support for reproduction and improvement.
Improvement must exceed the strongest relevant author comparator under predeclared meaningful gain and dependence-aware uncertainty; neither significance nor a changed endpoint counts.
Report paper_data and paper_data_author_code separately; source/runtime/execution/results remain unqualified and all four scientific outcomes unknown until evidence resolves the declared gates.
Retain historical biological findings separately; this explicit new scope does not retroactively qualify prior runs or claim whole-paper/current-SOTA superiority.
